doc.title: Jack Lesberg interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 11, 1997

chapter: Boston youth and learning the bass
title: The Coconut Grove fire and arriving in New York
summary: He worked the Coconut Grove in Boston, was carried out unconscious in the 1942 fire and spent a month in hospital, then went to New York in 1944.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Learning your horn: teachers, lessons and fees

blocks.x: I was carried out of there. I was carried out unconscious and I was quite ill there, in the hospital for about a month or so. And I survived it fine and my lungs and everything cleared out and I made my way out of there. And at this time I was already playing the bass, because I’d been playing floor shows there with it and doing all kinds of other things. And I didn’t really start studying the bass formally — I did have this other training, I studied the piano as well early when I was a kid. And when I got to New York — I went to New York in about 1944, and there was this marvelous array of teachers and everything, and amongst them was Fred Zimmermann, one of the best. And that was the way to go. I just inquired around and I went to him and I studied with him for about seven years. And we got along famously. He was very, very wonderful and dedicated teacher, a young guy, and young acting, one of those kind of guys. And he taught practically everybody. He taught at Juilliard as well. But I studied privately with him, and I was lucky enough to have him for several years. Quite a few, almost all the bass players went to him. He was that good.
